svg.text: Verified fault · decided by the rule table

text.tspan: My rule starts at
, so this is a clear reading

svg.text: Dashed means pointed to, not measured. Solid means measured.

text.tspan: At address you set up well: knees flexed, back tilted over the ball. The
trouble starts on the way down. When your hips move toward the ball, your
arms lose their room, so your chest stands up to make space. That is where
thin and blocked shots come from. I can’t measure hip mobility directly, so
treat the first link as a strong hint, not a fact.
One drill for the range, one exercise for home. That’s
enough for this week.

svg.text: Works on: hips move toward the ball

text.tspan: Set up with your backside touching a wall
or your golf bag. Swing slowly and keep
your trail glute on the wall through
impact.
If the glute leaves the wall, your hips moved
toward the ball.
Sit with both knees bent to 90°. Turn
slowly from one side to the other with
your chest tall.
Generic guidance, not medical advice —
see a physiotherapist if you feel pain.
Ask me about this swing. I answer only from what I
measured here.
Why does it feel like I’m staying down
when I’m not?
